kalejunkie HIDDEN VEGGIE PASTINA aka italian penicillin, the soup that cures all—sickness, a broken heart, and pays your bills for you too 😏. The real question is what can’t it do? This version sneaks in veggies for more fiber and flavor and if you have picky kids like me, they’ll never know it’s in there 🤝. 

SAVE this post! SHARE it with friends! And hello, FOLLOW ME kalejunkie if you want to see more easy delicious recipes in your feed (who wouldn’t, duh! 🙆🏻‍♀️)

Makes 6-8 servings
8 cups chicken broth (I used bone broth for more protein and nutrients!)
3 large carrots, peeled and halved
4 stalks celery, halved
1 yellow onion, roughly chopped
3 cloves garlic
2 tb betterthanbouillon chicken bouillon paste (or similar)
1 parmesan rind
2 bay leaves 
1 1/2 cups uncooked pastina (any small pasta shape like stelline or acini di pepe)
1 tsp turmeric
1 tsp kosher salt
1/2 cup freshly grated parmigiano reggiano cheese
Pepper and lemon juice to taste

In a large pot, add the broth, carrots, celery, onion, garlic, bouillon, parmesan rind, and bay leaves. Turn heat to medium-high. Bring to a gentle boil, then cover and reduce heat to medium and cook for 25 minutes or until carrots have softened. While the broth is cooking, bring another pot of water to a boil and cook pasta until al dente. Drain and set aside. Next, remove all the veggies from the pot and transfer to a blender. Add 1-2 cups of the broth as well as the turmeric and salt. Blend until smooth and return the mixture to the pot and stir until incorporated. To serve, divide the cooked pasta to bowls. Ingredients:

24 ounces bread, cut into ½-inch cubes (about 12 cups), preferably crusty sourdough or country bread

½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper

1 teaspoon chopped fresh rosemary

2 large eggs, beaten

Instructions:

- Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13-inch baking dish with 1½ tablespoons of butter.
- Spread the bread cubes in a single layer on a large baking sheet. Bake for 10 to 25 minutes, or until dry and crisp. Remove from the oven and transfer to a large bowl.
- Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion, celery, garlic, salt, and pepper and cook for 5 to 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, or until softened.
- Pour the onion mixture over the bread and sprinkle with the sage, parsley, rosemary, and thyme. Toss to coat. Add the broth and eggs and toss again. The bread should feel pretty wet. If it’s still a bit dry, add more broth as needed to moisten it. I often add another ¼ to ½ cup at this point.

I post this every autumn. It looks meaty – and tastes it too – but there’s no meat or even any mushrooms in it, just the humble little lentil. The pasta is cooked with the lentils and the starch produces a kind of stew. Lovely - inexpensive too.

AUTUMN PASTA WITH LENTILS
SERVES 4

2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, plus a little extra for drizzling
1 medium onion, finely chopped
2 clove garlic, grated to a purée
¼ tsp chilli flakes
1 carrot, finely chopped
1 stick celery, finely chopped
225g green lentils, washed well in a sieve
1 tbsp tomato purée
2 bay leaves
4 sprigs thyme
400g can chopped tomatoes (I use Mutti polpa)
8 cherry tomatoes
250g macaroni, or another pasta shape of similar size
15g Parmigiano Reggiano, grated, plus extra for serving

Heat the oil in a large saucepan and sauté the onion for 5-8 minutes over a medium heat, until quite soft. It shouldn’t get too much colour. Add the garlic and chilli flakes and cook for a couple of minutes more, then add the carrot, celery, lentils, tomato purée, herbs, seasoning and 1.2L water. Simmer the lentils, with the lid half off, for about 30 minutes. The lentils should keep their shape. Tip the can of tomatoes and the cherry tomatoes into the pan (leave the tomatoes whole to give a bit of texture and structure). Add the pasta, season again and add more water if you think the dish needs it.

Simmer for 10-15 minutes, uncovered, until the pasta is tender, stirring often so that the pasta releases its starch – you want to end up with a dish that is quite thick, not a soup. Add a little more water if you think the dish needs it.

Add the cheese and check the seasoning once more. Stir in some more extra virgin olive oil or drizzle it over individual servings. This can be reheated the next day – it still tastes great.
